questions.stem: Which stage does a Prototype follow?
options: Production
POC
UAT
SIT
MVP
questions.explanation: A Prototype is the next stage after the POC, once the POC has shown that the idea is feasible.

questions.stem: What comes into the picture at the Prototype stage?
options: Tools and technologies, where ideas start being converted into reality
Full production infrastructure and licences
Real business users working with live data
External regulatory audits
Complete business requirements and a signed SOW
questions.explanation: In prototyping, tools and technologies come into the picture and one starts converting ideas into reality.

options: Whether the idea is feasible for the first time
The cost of the production licences
How the end result and the product will look, the real end solution
The results of user acceptance testing
The final regulatory compliance report
questions.explanation: A Prototype shows how the end result will look, how the product will look, and the real end solution.

questions.stem: Is a Prototype built expecting business users to jump in and start using it?
options: Yes, business users are the main audience of a Prototype
Yes, a Prototype is released to all customers
Yes, but only after UAT
No, a Prototype is not built considering that business users will start using it
No, because a Prototype has no user interface
questions.explanation: A Prototype is not built considering that business users will jump in and start using it; it is for technical folks to evaluate.

questions.stem: For whom is a Prototype built and run?
options: Business users
External customers
Sales teams
Regulators
Technical users
questions.explanation: A Prototype is built and run for technical users.

questions.stem: What kind of data is normally used in a Prototype?
options: Dummy but relevant data
Full production data
No data at all
Anonymised data of full production size
Live streaming data from customers
questions.explanation: Prototypes are normally for technical folks to evaluate the end results with dummy but relevant data.

questions.stem: What has already been established by the time a Prototype begins?
options: That the production environment is ready
That the idea is feasible and will benefit the business agenda
That business users have accepted the solution
That SIT and UAT have passed
That the SOW has been signed
questions.explanation: In the POC one has tested that the idea is feasible and will benefit the business agenda; the Prototype then converts the idea into reality.

questions.stem: Which of the following is NOT true of a Prototype?
options: It follows the POC stage
It brings tools and technologies into the picture
It is released to actual business users to start using
It shows how the product will look
It uses dummy but relevant data
questions.explanation: A Prototype is not built for business users to start using; it is for technical users to evaluate the end result.

questions.stem: What is the purpose of the technical evaluation performed in a Prototype?
options: To calculate the annual budget
To sign off the production release
To train the sales team
To evaluate the end results using dummy but relevant data
To measure customer satisfaction
questions.explanation: Prototypes let technical folks evaluate the end results with dummy but relevant data.

questions.stem: How do a POC and a Prototype differ in audience?
options: Both are for business users
Both are for technical users
A POC is for regulators, a Prototype is for customers
A POC is for technical users, a Prototype is for business users
A POC is for business users, a Prototype is for technical users
questions.explanation: A POC is built and run for business users, whereas a Prototype is built and run for technical users.
